ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a grouped bar chart, with the vertical axis labeled "Amount of CFTR protein". The horizontal axis has two groups of cells: Normal cells and CF cells. The legend shows three locations: ER (light-colored bar), Vesicles (medium gray bar), Golgi (dark gray bar). In the Normal cells group, the amount of CFTR protein in the ER is relatively high, and there is also an obvious amount of CFTR protein in Vesicles and Golgi. In the CF cells group, the amount of CFTR protein in the ER is likewise relatively high, but the amount in Vesicles is very low, and the amount in Golgi is also very low. Reasoning: If CFTR protein is normally packaged and transported after synthesis, it should be able to appear at relatively high levels in vesicles and the Golgi apparatus. In normal cells, CFTR appears in Vesicles and Golgi, indicating that it is packaged and transported; whereas in CF cells, CFTR mainly remains in the ER, and there is very little in Vesicles and Golgi, indicating that it has not been effectively packaged into transport vesicles in the cytoplasm. Therefore, the correct statement is CFTR protein is not being packaged in the cytoplasm.
